title: Lakan 1 cassava (Lakan): Characteristics
metaDescription: Lakan 1 cassava is an all purpose cassava variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Lakan 1 cassava is an all purpose cassava variety, also sold or known as Lakan or Lakan cassava. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources.

heroImage.alt: Kamote vines on long raised ridges in San Rafael, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Lakan 1 cassava is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Lakan or Lakan cassava, this is the same cassava. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [cassava variety finder](/crop-varieties/cassava), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

The registry gives no day count or trial yield for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
It is recommended food, starch, feed.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 44.14 t/ha in a Bukidnon advanced yield trial, 47.61 t/ha with full NPK in Agusan del Sur.
**Where:** Grown nationwide, over 1,000 ha in Negros Occidental supplied a starch mill in the 1990s.
Recommended for food in the DA Northern Mindanao trial.
Used as the national check in variety selection.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: with Golden Yellow, the main cassava planted by Filipino farmers and the check variety breeders measure new clones against. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Lakan 1 cassava

Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Lakan the same as Lakan 1?
items.a: Yes. Lakan is another name for Lakan 1. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Lakan 1?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
